name: Lille Airport
before:
The airport for Lille, in the commune of Lesquin about 7 km south south east of the city, which is why it also goes by Lille-Lesquin. The run into the centre takes about fifteen minutes, and a shuttle bus connects the terminal with Lille Flandres railway station.

It is twelfth busiest in France by passengers, handling 1,397,637 in 2012 against around 970,000 in 2001. The passenger terminal dates from 1996.

Freight is where it punches above its weight. The airport is fourth in France for cargo, with almost 38,000 tonnes passing through each year.

Lille itself is the principal city of the Lille Métropole, the capital of the Hauts-de-France region and the prefecture of the Nord department, so this is a working airport for the whole of the north.
after:
The airport for Lille, in the commune of Lesquin about 7 km south south east of the city, which is why it also goes by Lille-Lesquin. A shuttle bus connects the terminal with Lille Flandres railway station, and the airport puts the average trip at 20 minutes.

The French airports' association ranks it eleventh in France, with about 1.7 million passengers in 2025. Its passenger terminal dates from 1996.

Lille itself is the capital of the Hauts-de-France region, so this is a working airport for the whole of the north.
